newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jordan King to West Bank as talks at impasse.
newsitem.headline: Jordan King to West Bank as talks at impasse.

text.p: Palestinians and Israelis split sharply on whether talks on a long-delayed Israeli redeployment in Hebron were fruitful as Jordan's King Hussein was due in the West Bank for the first time in 29 years to show solidarity with the Palestinians.

"There are a lot of difficulties, they (Israelis) are not intending to implement accurately and honestly what had been agreed upon and what had been signed," Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said in Jordan.

But a senior aide to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sounded a positive note: "Progress has been made. Things look good, things look promising," the adviser, who asked not to be named, told Reuters. He said Arafat and Netanyahu could meet to hammer out a final agreement on Hebron "within a few days".

Hussein, who hosted Arafat in Amman on Monday, was to fly with the Palestinian president on Tuesday to self-ruled Jericho in the West Bank. The Jordanian monarch has not set foot in the territory since he lost it to Israel in 1967.
King Hussein, Israel's closest Arab ally since Jordan signed a peace treaty in 1994, has stepped up public support of Arafat in recent days while distancing himself from Netanyahu.

Negotiators and diplomats battled in Jerusalem and Amman late on Monday to break an impasse over the Hebron pullback while the fate of formal U.S.-brokered talks slated for Tuesday in Egypt's Red Sea resort of Taba remained unclear.

Palestinian chief negotiator Saeb Erekat, who held informal talks with Israeli counterpart Lieutenant-General Dan Shomron at a Jerusalem hotel on Monday, said Israel's desire to modify the Hebron accord would deal a "total knockout" to the deal agreed to by Israel's previous government.

"Mr Netanyahu insists on opening the agreement. He wants for instance the right of Israeli troops to enter Hebron, or hot pursuit'. That is a total knockout to the agreement," Erekat told Israeli Channel One television.
Netanyahu seeks modifications in the Hebron deal in order to safeguard 400 Jews living in heavily-armed compounds amidst 100,000 Palestinians in Hebron.
U.S. Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross rushed to meet Arafat in Amman late on Monday to try to bridge the gaps between the sides.

Senior Arafat aide Khaled Salam told Reuters the Palestinian leader had instructed Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) negotiators to travel to Taba on Tuesday for the formal U.S.-mediated talks, but Israeli security sources said it was not clear whether the Israeli team would meet them there.

"The Palestinian delegation...has received urgent instructions from President Arafat to travel tonight to Taba," Salam told Reuters. "These instructions are in line with Palestinian commitments to the agreement with the Israeli and American sides that talks would start on Tuesday."
The formal Taba talks were to have resumed on Monday but were pushed back to allow the sides to progress in informal negotiation channels.
Salam said Israel sought to change the venue of the talks.
"We are simply looking where it is better and more comfortable to continue the talks," Shomron told Israel television.
